head.name: @fzlt/core/math
head.lead: Trig that gives the same bits on every engine, for anything that steps a sim. sin, cos, atan, atan2 and hypot from + − × ÷, Math.sqrt, Math.abs, Math.trunc and % (all exact, so the same everywhere) and bit reads only. The builtins may differ between engines in the last bit (WebKit calls the system's libm), and one bit in a heading is a different game online: a desync. These are fdlibm 5.3's algorithms (k_sin.c, k_cos.c, s_sin.c, s_cos.c, the medium path of e_rem_pio2.c, s_atan.c, e_atan2.c), the ones V8 ports for its Math.sin, cos, atan and atan2: in Node they return what the builtins return, bit for bit (tests/math.test.mjs), so a sim tested headless keeps its numbers; in Chromium and WebKit they return the same bits as in Node (tests/math-engines.mjs), while those browsers' own builtins differ from them (measured on Chromium 153 and WebKit 26: about 3% of sin and cos results and 18% of atan2's). hypot is V8's two-argument Math.hypot, written out (moved here from @fzlt/core/steer, which re-exports it). One limit: past |x| = 2^20·π/2 (about 1.6 million radians) fdlibm's exact reduction needs a big table; here such an x is first taken mod 2π (% is exact), so every engine still agrees, but V8's builtin may differ there. No game needs an angle that large. Rendering may keep the builtins (a pixel off is fine). Allocation-free wherever they are called from: a double returned from a call the JIT does not inline is boxed (a heap number each call), and so are its double arguments, and fdlibm's bodies are past V8's inlining limit: so the bodies take their arguments from one shared buffer and leave their result in another, and each export is a tiny wrapper (write, call, read) that always inlines. Shared buffers for the bit reads and the reduced argument too; every export tree-shakes on its own.

sizesNote: Measured on this build: minified and gzipped with everything it imports, the way npm run size checks the budget in CI.

blocks.label: NPM · @fzlt/core
blocks.code:
npm install @fzlt/core
import { sin, cos, atan, atan2, … } from "@fzlt/core/math";

blocks.label: IN SHORT
blocks.code:
const a = atan2(ty - y, tx - x); // in a step: the same bits on an iPhone and a desktop
x += cos(a) * v * dt; y += sin(a) * v * dt;

items.doc: Math.hypot of two numbers, without the builtin call: V8 boxes Math.hypot's arguments, a heap number per call in a hot loop. Same steps as V8's own (Infinity wins over NaN, scale by the larger, sum, sqrt), so it returns the same bits (tested against Math.hypot).
